title: Yami Gautam Urges Media Not to Alter Her Photos With AI: 'Should Not Be Done'
excerpt: The National Film Award winner asked outlets to use her photographs in original form, a day after Jr NTR condemned an AI-manipulated video of the 'Chuttamalle' song.
body:
• Yami Gautam posted on X on October 4 asking the media to "refrain from using AI to alter or enhance" her photographs from public appearances and to use images "in original form."
  • Her statement goes beyond condemning malicious deepfakes: even seemingly benign AI enhancements of a person's likeness, she said, "should not be done without their knowledge and consent."
  • The post came a day after Jr NTR condemned an AI-manipulated version of the "Chuttamalle" song from Devara: Part 1 and warned of legal action; Chiranjeevi and Vijay Deverakonda have also spoken out.
  • India currently has no dedicated law on deepfakes; the government has signaled it will address the issue through pending digital legislation.

Mumbai: Yami Gautam has drawn a line on artificial intelligence and celebrity images. In a post on X on October 4, the actor asked the media to stop using AI to alter or enhance her photographs — and framed consent as the dividing line.

"A sincere request to the media," she wrote. "Please refrain from using AI to alter or enhance my photographs from public appearances. Kindly use images in original form. Altering or manipulating an individual's image or likeness using AI should not be done without their knowledge and consent. Thank you in advance for respecting my request!"

"Altering or manipulating an individual's image or likeness using AI should not be done without their knowledge and consent."

— Yami Gautam, on X

The request is addressed specifically to the media, though some outlets have paraphrased it as aimed at netizens and fans as well. Gautam did not name any specific incident that prompted the statement.

The trigger

The timing is hard to miss. A day earlier, Jr NTR publicly condemned an AI-manipulated video of the "Chuttamalle" song from Devara: Part 1 — a digitally altered version surfaced online featuring Janhvi Kapoor alongside Jr NTR, with explicit imagery not present in the original. On Saturday, October 3, he denounced the fake and warned of legal action against those who created and spread it.

https://x.com/RVCJ_FB/status/2106641932634247410

Chiranjeevi and Vijay Deverakonda also took to social media to denounce the misuse of AI to alter celebrity images and videos, turning what began as one fake video into an industry-wide flashpoint.

Consent, not just malice

Gautam's framing is broader than the deepfake debate that triggered it. By objecting to "alter or enhance" — language that covers routine editorial retouching as well as synthetic manipulation — she argues that even aesthetic AI changes to a likeness are an image-rights violation without consent. Digital-rights advocates have made the same case: once AI can redraw a face at scale, the boundary between benign enhancement and manipulation collapses.

The legal backdrop is thin. India has no dedicated law on deepfakes; existing provisions on defamation, obscenity and impersonation under the IT Act apply unevenly, and the government has signaled it will address AI-generated misinformation through pending digital legislation.

What's next for Gautam

The statement arrives at a high point in her career. Gautam won the National Film Award for Best Actress at the 72nd National Film Awards, announced September 22, for Article 370, produced by her husband Aditya Dhar; the film also won Best Feature Film.

Her next release, Nayyi Navelli — directed by Balaji Mohan and produced by Aanand L Rai and Himanshu Sharma's Colour Yellow Productions with Amazon MGM Studios — arrives October 16, ahead of Dussehra. She plays Mohini, a new daughter-in-law in the Awasthi family. Whether the industry follows her lead on AI-altered imagery may now be the more consequential release date.
